t: , That section 39(a) of the Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act of the District of Columbia (D.C. Code, sec. 40—455(a)) is amended by striking out “trial for” and all that follows down through “the operating privilege” and inserting in lieu thereof “trial for driving a motor vehicle within the District of Columbia at a time when his license is suspended or revoked, the operating privilege”.

fable.w: This section is a purely textual amendment to a District of Columbia motor vehicle statute concerning driving with a suspended or revoked license. The word "trial" might suggest litigation, but it refers to a person's trial for a driving offense, not a right to sue over or take part in a federal decision. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to object, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, or advisory body.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “trial for” and all that follows down through “the operating privilege” and inserting in lieu thereof

opus.w: This is a technical amendment to the D.C. Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act. It changes which criminal trial leads to the loss of a driver's operating privilege. A criminal trial of a defendant is not outsiders being consulted before a federal decision, and the amendment creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty, or right to sue. Mentioning a 'trial' only describes an enforcement step, not participation.
opus.s: trial for driving a motor vehicle within the District of Columbia at a time when his license is suspended or revoked, the operating privilege

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment that modifies the text of a District of Columbia code regarding license suspensions. It does not create any mechanism for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with, comment to, or participate in federal decision-making. It is purely a change in statutory language defining an offense.
qwen_chat.s: That section 39(a) of the Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act of the District of Columbia (D.C. Code, sec. 40—455(a)) is amended by striking out “trial for” and all that follows down through “the operating privilege” and inserting in lieu thereof “trial for driving a motor vehicle within the District of Columbia at a time when his license is suspended or revoked, the operating privilege”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that amending a statute regarding license suspensions involves public participation because it affects drivers. However, the text itself is merely a legislative amendment instruction; it does not establish any process for the public to consult with the government, comment on rules, or participate in decision-making. It simply changes the legal definition of an offense.
